scope: Separated coloured paths, missing cells, endpoint/corner repairs, ray redirection, and directly decodable pairwise layer cues.
known_limitations: The solver assumes each colour is one path and that paths are 1-cell wide polylines with perpendicular turns. Same-colour duplicates or colinear consecutive segments are outside its model.

Path rebuild relies on generator-style separation: same-colour pieces and 2s at least 3 apart, and no touching strands beyond what the bridge veto handles. Arbitrary touching configurations could create spurious or missing runs.
Marker K must be a true corner with exactly one perpendicular kept neighbour. Markers at path ends, at straight cells, or on closed loops raise SceneContradictionError.

Layer decoding encodes the generator's fitted cue semantics. If the real ARC rule differs, for example a loose blank resolved by the reference program's longer-path tie-break, the solver raises SceneAmbiguityError instead of guessing. It does not reproduce that tie-break.
The input colour at ray crossings is not checked against the expected lower path. Cells with values other than 0 or the two crossing colours are treated as uninformative.
Mixed visible cues on an unanchored pair, ray-ray crossings, triple overlaps and cyclic layer cues raise errors. These never occur in valid generator scenes but could occur in hand-made inputs.

findings: Scope: this artifact covers only faa9f03d. No generator or fixtures for cbebaa4b (connector assembly) or d8e07eb2 (catalogue-driven joint piece assembly) were supplied, so I make no findings or code for them.

Hand trace: I traced all 4 train pairs and the test pair through the solver by hand. Path rebuild, marker resolution and layer decoding reproduce the canonical outputs at every changed cell, including (2,1) and (2,6) in demo 4 and (7,1), (7,7) and (7,10) in the test. Nothing was executed.

Path rebuild: path cells are rebuilt from pixels only. Each row and column is scanned, with colour-or-2 counted as on. Single gaps are bridged unless a neighbouring real cell has both perpendicular neighbours on (the same veto as the generator's _bridges_ok). A run is kept only with at least 2 real cells.

Why the rebuild is exact in random mode: _holes_ok forbids holes at segment ends and adjacent holes, and a crossing showing the other colour counts as a hole. _spacing_ok keeps same-colour pieces and every 2 at least 3 apart on a line. So the latent cells are recovered exactly.
Where the bridge veto matters: it is only needed for fixtures. Demo 2 column 4, where (5,4) and (7,4) must not merge, and test column 1 for colour 6 rely on it.

Marker resolution, rule: a 4 at M selects K = the adjacent rebuilt corner whose limb O = 2K - M continues straight away from the 4. The limb is deleted as the component of the path minus K that contains O. The ray runs from K through M to the edge.

Marker resolution, coverage: random mode keeps every neighbour of M except K off all paths, so K is trivially unique there. Demo 2 is different: the 4 at (2,9) also touches 7 at (2,10). Only the limb and corner test resolves it. Random mode never generates this marker-next-to-a-foreign-path configuration, nor a ray that crosses on its second cell.
Layering, ray crossings: decoding follows the generator's documented display semantics. A ray crossing fixes the ray path as upper; the input shows the crossed path there.

Layering, blank crossings: a blank crossing with a decided marker-axis preference is always the true upper path. _decorate only blanks when pref == top, so these blanks are trustworthy anchors. Blanks with no decided preference carry no information.

Layering, visible crossings: on unanchored pairs, visible crossings always show the lower path. Only anchored pairs may show the upper colour (type d, demo 4 (2,1)), so the solver ignores visible cues there.

Layer cues in random mode are always direct. The settled fallback guarantees every final crossing pair has at least one decisive cue. Each cell holds at most two paths, so five-path scenes reduce to independent pairwise decisions.

Untested layer paths: random mode never needs transitive inference or the reference program's longer-path tie-break. The solver uses transitive closure only as a sound fallback. It raises an error rather than applying a length tie-break.

Generator simplification, damage: 2s are placed only at path vertices (ends and corners), never at crossings. The explanation's phrase 'or where two paths meet' is not realised by the generator. Gaps are 1-4 single interior non-crossing cells and are never on ray crossings.

Generator simplification, strands: random mode forbids touching strands of different colours. All demos contain them: demo 1 columns 3 and 4 at rows 3-5, demo 2 (9,8)/(10,8) and the 4 beside the 7-column. So fresh scenes never test the bridge veto or marker disambiguation.

Generator simplification, rays: rays never cross other rays, deleted limbs, vertices or existing crossings. They never pass next to their own path, and never stop at an obstacle. Every ray is a clean straight extension to the edge that lies above everything it crosses.

Uncertain rule: the four-type crossing display is a synthetic, decodable cue system fitted to five demonstrations. The explanation itself calls the real layer rule its least transparent part. In particular, the rule that a blank overrides a visible cue (demo 4) is an interpretation, not an independently confirmed ARC rule.
Ignored cells: crossings on deleted limbs may show either colour or be blank, and they are ignored. Removing the limb removes that crossing from the output.

No search: the decode is deterministic, so budget exhaustion cannot occur. Outcomes are unique, ambiguous (SceneAmbiguityError), or contradiction (SceneContradictionError). solve_with_status reports which one occurred.
semantic_review.execution_evidence: All five canonical fixtures and 1000 fresh unique scenes match both the independently implemented solver and saved reference.
semantic_review.caution: The synthetic crossing display is a documented hypothesis fitted to supplied cases, not exhaustive coverage of all possible path-interaction semantics.
